conventions.convention: Colored links are finite, oriented, smoothly embedded in S³, with a homotopy class of nowhere-zero normal field on each component. Evaluation assumes countable choice, takes values in End(1), and assigns the empty link 1₁.
A = ω⁻², q_K = A², q_L = A⁻², and K_L = K_K⁻¹. The selected categorical twist is X² = −A³I, rather than the usual quantum-group ribbon convention; the quantum dimension is δ = −A² − A⁻².
The fundamental positive Artin crossing has height increasing upward and the right input strand passing over the left input strand.

The matrix procedure uses n ≥ 1, composition-order reading, adjacent color swaps, identity-position closure pairing, and rejection when the final color tuple differs from the initial tuple. Its pivotal comparison is j = uθ.

Positive stabilization inserts θ_X = λI and increases exponent sum by one. The unframed correction is λ⁻ʷtₙ, assumes AC, uses one absolutely simple color on every component, and includes no categorical-dimension normalization.
The bracket has unknot value 1, whereas the fundamental ribbon trace has unknot value δ. Their Hecke specialization is v = A⁻⁴ and z = −1/(A⁻⁴ + 1).

load_bearing.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. For a ribbon category with chosen left duals, RT_C(L) := F_C(L) lies in End_C(1), depends only on the framed colored isotopy class, and assigns the empty link 1₁.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. In a k-linear ribbon category with k-bilinear tensor product and End_C(1) = k, an absolutely simple color X has twist θ_X = λid_X, and λ⁻ʷ⁽ᵝ⁾tₙ(β) depends only on the oriented unframed link type when every component has color X. No categorical-dimension normalization is asserted.

For supplied finite matrix ribbon data, read a finite braid word while swapping adjacent colors; use the displayed adjacent braiding for a positive letter, and 'for a negative letter use its inverse'; reject unequal final and initial color tuples, otherwise return ev_{W∨}((J_W M_β) ⊗ 1)coev_W.

Over Q(ω), with A = ω⁻², q_K = A² and q_L = A⁻², the fundamental module has the displayed positive braiding, scalar categorical twist −A³I, quantum dimension −A² − A⁻², and specified self-dual maps B and U.

Assume countable choice. For every n ≥ 1 and β ∈ Bₙ, tₙ(β) = δ⟨β̂⟩ = δⁿ(−A)ʷ⁽ᵝ⁾trₙ(πₙ(β)) specialized at v = A⁻⁴ and z = −1/(A⁻⁴ + 1). Multiplication by (−A³)⁻ʷ gives the stated value-by-value normalization identity.

concerns.concern: Definition lines 31–33 specify c_{V_ai,V_ai+1} for the current adjacent colors and then say 'for a negative letter use its inverse.' For current colors A,B, that inverse has source B⊗A, whereas the required negative crossing has source A⊗B and is c_{B,A}⁻¹. Thus the literal instruction is ill-typed for unequal colors; a two-strand word σ₁⁻² with initial tuple (A,B) passes the final-color test but already encounters the wrong source at its first letter. Proof 1.1 repeats 'its typed inverse' without supplying the reversed subscripts. The general correctness assertion in thm-ribbon-evaluation-from-colored-braid-word-procedure-properties consequently needs the same review. Constant-color consumers avoid this particular defect.

Proof 1.4 concludes 'The closed loop is B(U(1))=... Thus these maps give ... quantum dimension.' The left-duality snakes alone do not identify B with the ribbon-induced opposite cap used in the pivotal closure. Here the missing check is elementary: the published evaluator's formula gives that cap as B c_{V,V}(θ_V⊗1), and the supplied matrices give B c_{V,V}(−A³I⊗1)=B. This establishes the claimed dimension, but the identification is unstated and is subsequently used by the ribbon/bracket lemma.

alerts.finding: alg-colored-jones-from-ribbon-evaluation lines 43–57 say 'The positive generator convention is the braid-height convention used by the matrix c_N: strand i+1 passes over strand i' and draw downward arrows with the top-right strand continuously overpassing the top-left strand. This is the opposite crossing sign from the supplied fundamental convention: def-quantum-sl2-fundamental-ribbon-module draws the same matrix with upward arrows and the bottom-right strand overpassing, and def-oriented-crossing-sign-writhe-and-blackboard-framing fixes positive projection coordinates (t,x). In those coordinates the downstream downward drawing has negative determinant for (over tangent, under tangent); rotating the supplier drawing by 180 degrees instead gives a downward drawing with the top-left strand overpassing. At N=2 the displayed c_N is exactly the supplier matrix, so the diagram's claimed positive sign is inconsistent with its cited convention. The matrix instructions themselves need not share the diagram defect.

seams_checked.note: The ribbon/bracket lemma preserves n ≥ 1, the positive crossing chart, bracket unknot value 1, the extra δ factor in the ribbon trace, and the exact Hecke specialization. It expressly avoids claiming a Jones specialization from the normalization identity alone.

This is a declared page prerequisite without a BMW/Dubrovnik item proposition invoked by the assigned ribbon items. The inspected Dubrovnik conventions use their own parameters and normalization; the ribbon page makes no identification that strengthens or changes those claims.

The scalar-twist and finite-evaluation citations preserve their hypotheses, including AC, absolute simplicity, effective finite matrices, and generic dimension normalization. Constant-color calls avoid the mixed-color inverse issue. However, the downstream algorithm claims the supplied positive-crossing convention while drawing its opposite sign; the exact discrepancy is recorded in alerts.
